items.title: R Sreelekha’s resignation bid puts ruling BJP in trouble at Tvm Corporation
items.summary: Putting the Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled Thiruvananthapuram Corporation in deep trouble, councillor and former Director General of Police R Sreelekha has submitted her resignation letter to Mayor V V Rajesh, citing personal reasons. The resignation, however, has not been official yet as the letter has to be ideally submitted to the Corporation secretary as per the Kerala Municipality Act (KMA). The resignation move is a major setback to the BJP, which has been ruling the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation with a razor-thin majority. The BJP currently rules the 101-member Corporation with 50 councillors, backed by an independent councillor. If the resignation is accepted, the number of BJP councillors will drop to 49. As per reports, Sreelekha submitted the resignation letter to the Mayor on September 30. However, the incident came out only on Saturday, October 3, when the retired Indian Police Service (IPS) officer announced it in a WhatsApp group related to her ward. In the message, Sreelekha added that she would submit the resignation letter to the district collector on Monday. items.title: Kerala High Court stays trial against Sriram Venkitaraman IAS in rash driving case
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday stayed the further proceedings in the criminal trial against IAS officer Sriram Venkitaraman in connection with the 2019 rash driving case against him [ Jaseela C v State of Kerala & ors ]. The case involves allegations that Venkitaraman recklessly drove his car while under the influence of alcohol and rammed it into a motorcycle driver by journalist KM Basheer, resulting in Basheer’s death. Basheer's widow, Jaseela C, has now filed a plea challenging the State government's decision not to appoint a Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) to conduct the trial, despite an earlier assurance to do so. Justice G Girish briefly heard the plea today and sought the State's response on why it has refused to appoint an SPP to conduct the trial. The Court proceeded to stay the trial proceedings as well for now. Justice G Girish Venkitaraman presently is facing trial for offences such as rash and negligent driving, causing death by a negligent act, and driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs under the Indian Penal Code and the Motor Vehicles Act. items.title: Buddhist activist moves Supreme Court against singing full version of Vande Mataram; terms it Islamophobic
items.summary: A petition has been filed before the Supreme Court challenging two Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) orders that mandate the singing of all six stanzas of national song Vande Mataram at formal State events [ BD Borkar v. Union of India ]. The petition has been moved by BD Borkar, a Nagpur-based Buddhist activist, Ambedkarite scholar and civil rights advocate. Drawing on anti-caste traditions, Borkar has contended that the MHA orders dated January 28, 2026, and July 9, 2026, illegally replace the 79-year-old practice of singing a standalone, non-theistic two-stanza poem with the full version containing explicit anti-Muslim invective. "Under the guise of providing directions on the playing and singing of an ‘official version’... the impugned orders repealed the existing National Song... and imposed a new National Song which is the six-stanza civil war song of Anandamath with its unconstitutional idolatrous and Islamophobic content," the plea states. As per the plea, for nearly eight decades since Independence, India peaceably adopted a standalone two-stanza version of Vande Mataram . Written in the early 1870s, this version pre-dates the novel Anandamath written by Bankim Chandra Chatte

items.title: Bombay High Court orders takedown of AI deepfakes, derogatory content against Samantha Ruth Prabhu
items.summary: The Bombay High Court today ordered the takedown of content found misusing the name, image and voice of actress Samantha Ruth Prabhu [ Samantha Ruth Prabhu v. John Doe & Ors ]. Justice Madhav Jamdar passed the interim order on a plea filed by Prabhu seeking the protection of her personality rights. The Court has restrained the publication of objectionable content that involve the unauthorised use of the name, image, and voice of the actress, including deepfakes created through the use of artificial intelligence. The Court passed the order after noting that the content flagged by Prabhu in her personality rights suit - including morphed content and deepfakes - demonstrated a prima facie violation of the actor's personality, publicity, and moral rights. “The plaintiff's (Samantha Prabhu's) personality rights and publicity rights are protected by Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution of India, that is, the right to freedom of speech and expression, as also by Article 21 of the Constitution of India, that is, the right to life and personal liberty, including the right to privacy and the right to human dignity, and her moral rights as a performer are separately protected under Section 38

items.title: Child custody cases: Karnataka High Court suggests replacing 'visitation' with 'parenting time'
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday expressed the need for change in the terminology employed in judicial proceedings that concern child custody. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti questioned how a trial court had passed an order that allowed the father to visit the child on weekends for 3-4 hours, 50% of school vacations and 30 minutes of call time on WhatsApp between 7:30 to 8:30 PM. Justice Kanneganti also said that courts must replace the phrase 'visitation time' with 'parenting time'. "Courts often use the word "visitation" to describe the time the child spends with a parent who is a non-custodial parent. The term is familiar, but it carries an unfortunate suggestion that one parent is part of the child's life while the other merely visits. A child should not be made to understand the relationship through the word "visitation," which is used for someone who arrives and leaves as a guest. Children read the conduct of adults and sometimes the words of Courts to understand where they belong. Calling it parenting time recognizes a simple truth that no parent is a visitor in the life of a child." items.title: 30-year-old NOIDA housing dispute: Supreme Court appoints former judge to identify genuine allottees
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently constituted a one-member high-powered independent committee headed by former Allahabad High Court Justice Sudhir Kumar Saxena to finalise the list of genuine members and subsequent purchasers entitled to multi-storeyed flats in NOIDA [ New Okhla Industrial Development Authority v. Kendriya Karamchari Sehkari GN Samiti & Ors. ] A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana constituted the committee on September 24 after observing that the verification process remained deadlocked despite repeated affidavits and directions. "Having regard to the fact that this process has remained inconclusive despite repeated affidavits and directions and considering that a large number of the original allottee-members have been awaiting the fruits of litigation for over three decades, we are satisfied that an independent verification mechanism to decide the competing claims and implement this Court’s earlier directions is necessary, " the Court ordered. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The dispute stemmed from a long sequence of litigation concerning the Kendriya Karamchari Sehkari GN Samiti.

items.title: Is slipping into DMs enough to prove adultery by wife? Allahabad High Court answers
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently said that a husband cannot merely rely on social media messages to establish that his wife is continuously “living in adultery” without corroborative evidence of physical intimacy or cohabitation. Justice Jai Krishna Upadhyay was dealing with a husband’s plea challenging the grant of maintenance to his wife. The husband’s primary argument was that his wife was disentitled from claiming any maintenance as she is “living in adultery”. In this regard, he placed reliance on printouts of Instagram chats alleged to have taken place between her and an advocate, with whom she is allegedly in an adulterous relationship. However, the Court said that the husband has to prove a continuous “adulterous lifestyle” of his wife to deny maintenance to her. It said that Instagram chats were not sufficient to establish the alleged adultery. “Even if, for the sake of argument, the contents of the unverified chats were to be perused, mere text messages on a social media platform, without corroborative evidence of physical intimacy or cohabitation, are thoroughly insufficient to legally establish that the wife is continuously "living in adultery",” the Court said. items.title: Body-shaming, verbal abuse not enough to prove offence of insulting woman’s modesty: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that allegations of body-shaming and verbally abusing another woman do not, by themselves, constitute the offence of insulting a woman’s modesty under Section 509 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Section 509 IPC criminalises words, sounds, gestures or acts intended to insult a woman’s modesty, as well as intrusions into her privacy. The provision prescribes a maximum sentence of 3 years’ imprisonment and a fine. Justice SR Krishna Kumar quashed criminal proceedings against two women, aged 25 and 27, accused of body-shaming and verbally abusing another woman in Bengaluru. “Having regard to the mandatory ingredients required to constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC, merely because the petitioners and accused No.3 (the women accused of body-shaming) are said to have bodyshamed the complainant and insulted her about her physical appearance, it cannot be said that the material on record discloses the commission of the offence punishable under Section 509 IPC,” the Court said. items.title: Gujarat High Court upholds judge's dismissal over 'benami' phones, undisclosed vehicle purchases
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court recently upheld the dismissal of a Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) from service over allegations that he held three 'benami' mobile phones, and that he had failed to disclose vehicle purchases and a personal loan in violation of applicable rules [ Amratlal Narendrabhai Vizoda vs State of Gujarat & Anr ]. A Division Bench of Justice NS Sanjay Gowda and Justice JL Odedra also noted that one of the 'benami' mobile phones used by the judicial officer was acquired from a practicing advocate, with whom he exchanged as many as 186 phonecalls between June 2007 and May 2008. The Court termed this improper conduct on the judicial officer's part. "A Judicial Officer should not associate himself with practicing advocates and has to maintain a distance from the advocates to prevent any impression of impropriety. If the evidence indicated that he had actually secured the phone from a practicing advocate and was using the same, that, by itself, clearly amounts to misconduct," the Bench observed. items.title: Sabarimala halal jaggery row: Kerala High Court tells Devaswom Board to exercise greater care
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday told the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) to exercise greater care while procuring supplies for making Nivedyam/ Prasadam at the Sabarimala temple after a plea raised objections to the use of halal certified jaggery in the preparations [SJR Kumar v The Travancore Devaswom Board & ors]. A Division Bench of Justices Raja Vijayaraghavan V and KV Jayakumar said that the board should have ensured that the supplies for the temple did not carry symbols or declaration that could create concerns over whether the materials complied with the religious customs followed at Sabarimala. " Ideally, the Travancore Devaswom Board ought to have exercised greater care to ensure that the quantity of jaggery supplied by the manufacturer did not bear symbols, markings or declarations that could give rise to an apprehension of conflict with the religious customs and practices followed at the Temple, " the Court added. The Court, however, found no issue with the quality of the jaggery as the laboratory reports showed that it was satisfactory and did not contain any substance or element that made it unsuitable for preparing Prasadam. items.title: Delhi High Court blocks ₹213 crore payout by SAIL to British company over unstamped arbitral award
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has blocked the release of over ₹213 crore deposited by Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) towards an arbitral award in favour of British Marine PLC after finding that the award was unstamped and could not presently be enforced. [British Marine v. SAIL] Justice Vinod Kumar held that an unstamped arbitral award is not executable and rejected British Marine's application seeking release of the balance amount deposited by SAIL. “ Unstamped Award would not be executable, therefore, the amount cannot be released to Decree Holder ,” the Court said The Court, however, clarified that British Marine could take steps to bring the original arbitral award before the High Court, pay the requisite stamp duty and, thereafter, move a fresh application for release of the money. Delhi HC judge Justice Vinod Kumar The case arose from an arbitral award passed in favour of British Marine, which had initiated enforcement proceedings before the Delhi High Court. SAIL had challenged the award under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. items.title: Common knowledge that data of Indians is traded on dark web: Supreme Court
items.summary: It is common knowledge that personal data of Indians is traded on the dark web, the Supreme Court said on Thursday. A Bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea moved by cybersecurity researcher Himanshu Pathak regarding alleged data vulnerabilities in the systems of Star Health and Allied Insurance Company. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana Representing Star Health, Senior Advocate S Muralidhar today assured the Court that the data being secured by the insurance company is secure, contrary to Pathak’s apprehensions. “ We have taken extraordinary security measures. Your Lordships will be quite astonished how many layers of security we have built. We do continuous monitoring now , ” Muralidhar said. “ But it is common knowledge that data of Indians is being traded on the dark web ,” pointed out Justice Bagchi. “ Dark web is something beyond the control of anyone, with the greatest respect. Just because there is a dark web, we cannot be complicit,” replied Muralidhar. Senior Advocate S Muralidhar Advocate Prashant Bhushan appeared for Pathak.
